name: Asahel
overview: Asahel was a male Levite known for being sent by King Jehoshaphat as a representative or official. His role is noted specifically in 2 Chronicles 17:8, indicating his involvement in the religious or administrative activities of the tribe of Levi during Jehoshaphat's reign. There are no additional notes elaborating on his life or deeds.
namesAndTitles: The name Asahel means 'G-d [El] has made,' reflecting a recognition of divine creation or provision. This proper name, recorded in 2 Chronicles 17:8, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful theistic significance consistent with Hebrew naming traditions.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Asahel as a descendant of the tribe of Levi, establishing his Levitical heritage. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Asahel's significance lies in his role as a Levite appointed by King Jehoshaphat, which suggests he was entrusted with responsibilities related to religious instruction or governance. His mention in 2 Chronicles 17:8 highlights the importance of Levites in supporting the spiritual reforms and administrative organization during Jehoshaphat's reign. This reflects the biblical emphasis on the Levites as servants of God within Israel's covenant community.
